reasons: Wrappers are simple and error messages are passed on.
The user's key is sent in the request body.

terms.meaning: the name of the document type requested from the server
improve an existing text according to a change instruction
the AI company that runs the model, such as Together AI, Anthropic or OpenAI

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and server rule
sections.what: Brings in the needed types and states that all AI work happens through the server.
sections.why: The header says this keeps the AI key on the server.
sections.watch_out: The provider key is still sent from the browser with each call, so it is not fully kept server-side.

sections.name: callGenerate
sections.title: Shared generation call
sections.what: The core helper that sends one request for a document type, with the profile, job, contact and research notes, and returns the server's data.
sections.why: Other helpers reuse it so the request is written once.
sections.watch_out: Errors show the server's message or only a status number, so details can be vague.

sections.name: generateTailoredResume
sections.title: Tailored resume
sections.what: Asks for a resume tailored to one job and returns its text.
sections.why: Wraps the resume action for the screens.
sections.watch_out: Only the text is returned; any structure in the reply is dropped.

sections.name: generateCoverLetter
sections.title: Cover letter
sections.what: Asks for a cover letter for one job and returns its text.
sections.why: Same pattern as the other document helpers.
sections.watch_out: If the server does not return a content field, the result is blank.

sections.name: generateExecutiveSummary
sections.title: Executive summary
sections.what: Asks for a short executive summary for one job and returns its text.
sections.why: Same pattern as the other document helpers.
sections.watch_out: Same content field dependency as the cover letter.

sections.name: generateProblemSolverPitch
sections.title: Problem solver pitch
sections.what: Asks for a pitch showing how the user solves a problem for a company, optionally using research notes about it.
sections.why: Research notes make the pitch specific to the company.
sections.watch_out: Without research notes, the pitch is more generic.

sections.name: generateHMOutreach
sections.title: Hiring manager message
sections.what: Asks for an outreach message to a hiring manager, optionally using that manager's details.
sections.why: Same pattern, with contact details added.
sections.watch_out: Without a contact, the message will not be personalised.

sections.name: generateLinkedInDM
sections.title: LinkedIn direct message
sections.what: Asks for a short LinkedIn message to a person, optionally personalised.
sections.why: Same pattern as the other outreach helpers.
sections.watch_out: Without a contact, the message will not be personalised.

sections.name: generateReferralDM
sections.title: Referral request message
sections.what: Asks for a message requesting a referral, which requires a named contact.
sections.why: A referral request needs a specific person, so the contact is required.
sections.watch_out: Callers must always supply a contact for this message.

sections.name: generateCEOColdEmail
sections.title: CEO cold email
sections.what: Asks for a cold email to a company's CEO, optionally using contact details.
sections.why: Same pattern as the other outreach helpers.
sections.watch_out: Without a contact, the email may be generic.

sections.name: generateSkillGap
sections.title: Skill gap analysis
sections.what: Asks for an analysis of skills the user lacks for a job and returns the structured result.
sections.why: Returns data rather than text, because the result is a list of gaps.
sections.watch_out: The server must return a data field; if it does not, nothing is returned.

sections.name: refineGeneration
sections.title: Refining existing text
sections.what: Sends existing text and a change request to the server and returns the improved version.
sections.why: Lets users edit a generated document without starting over.
sections.watch_out: The document type is sent in a header, so the server must read that header to apply the right rules.

summary: Browser-side helpers that ask the server to write resumes, cover letters, outreach messages and other documents for a job, and to refine existing text.
purpose: Gives each screen one simple function per document type.
why: The header states that all AI calls go through the server so the API key stays server-side.
how: 1. Each helper names the document type it wants. 2. The shared call sends the profile, job, optional contact and research notes to the generation route. 3. It adds the user's provider choice when it is not the default. 4. It returns the text or data from the reply, or throws an error with the server's message.
inputs: Profile, application, optional contact details, optional research notes, and for refinement the current text and an instruction.
outputs: Text for documents, structured data for skill gaps, or an error.
risks: The user's API key is sent from the browser in the request body with each call, so it is not fully kept server-side. Errors may show only a status number when the server gives no message.
debug: Open the browser network view and check the request to /api/generate. The action name must match a server action. A request failed message with a status points to the server logs.
